To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of montelukat and budesonide is more effective than budesonide and formoterol in preventing the expected deterioration in airway inflammation and function in children exposed to allergen.

in children with asthma, the use of formoterol or montelukast combined with budes-onide could be effective as add-on therapy to protect against the deterioration of pulmonary function and airway inflammation in asthmatic subjects exposed to relevant allergen.

montelukast and formoterol are equally effective in preventing the increase of inflammatory indices (eNO and sputum cells), but only montelukast is effective in preventing the deterioration of symptoms and lung function in asthmatic patients exposed to relevant allergen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of monteleukast and formoterol as a second-line treatment in children with allergic asthma exposed to relevant allergen.
the use of formoterol or montelukast added to budesonide for a short period of time in children exposed to relevant natural allergens.
the effects of formoterol and montelukast in asthmatic pediatric patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of budesonide plus formoterol is more effective than budesonide alone in preventing symptoms and airway hyperresponsiveness, whereas the combination of bdesonide plus montelukast has an additional protective effect on airway inflammation.
montelukast, as well as formoterol, is effective in protecting the airway inflammation induced by allergen exposure in children.
the addition of montelukat or formoterol to low-dose inhaled budesonide is an effective and safe strategy to prevent asthma deterioration caused by allergen exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in allergic asthmatic patients, the use of formoterol or montelukast added to low-doses of inhaled corticosteroids could offer a durable protection on symptoms, lung functions, and airway inflammatory markers.
montelukast is effective in reducing the expected increase of eNO after allergen exposure in asthmatic subjects.

in asthmatic patients with allergic sensitization, the use of a combination of inhaled corticosteroids with a long-acting beta(2) agonist or leukotriene receptor antagonist could offer a durable protection on the symptoms, lung function and inflammatory indices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
montelukast and formoterol, in addition to inhaled corticosteroids, may be useful for the control of asthma exacerbation in children.
the combination of montelukat and budesonide can prevent the expected increase in exhaled nitric oxide in asthmatic patients after exposure to relevant allergen.
in asthmatic patients exposed to relevant allergen, montelukast is more effective than formoterol in reducing the expected increase of eNO.
